budget.time_policy: caller-owned wall-clock cancellation; adapter performs no time-based stale-lock inference

determinism.accounting: root depth, path components, head bytes, content bytes, objects, events, artifacts, directory entries, temporary entries, read chunks, write chunks, and replay calls have fixed ceilings checked before corresponding traversal or allocation
determinism.canonicalization: logical store contents depend only on canonical command, event, artifact, revision, and store-head bytes; directory fan-out is lowercase full SHA-256, HEAD bytes are sorted compact ASCII JSON with one LF, and nondeterministic temporary names never enter content or result identity
determinism.identity: session path identity is SHA-256 of the canonical session ID UTF-8 bytes; content files use SHA-256 of exact bytes; store-head identity uses its canonical null-self-hash preimage; filesystem inode, device, mode, owner, path spelling, mtime, clock, PID, and checkout identity never become session identity
determinism.platform: logical successful contents and loaded core results are byte-identical across supported Python 3.10 through 3.14 and Linux, macOS, and Windows; platform-specific fsync availability may affect durability observation but never canonical bytes or authority
determinism.transaction: all immutable dependencies commit before one atomic HEAD replacement; lock acquisition serializes cooperating writers, exact expected-head comparison supplies optimistic concurrency, and recovery chooses only a fully replayable already committed HEAD

effects.filesystem: reads and writes only beneath the exact caller-supplied validated root; creates derived objects, events, revisions, sessions, locks, temporary files, and HEAD entries; never touches repository files, user configuration, arbitrary paths, or another session
effects.mutation: never mutates caller values or committed immutable object bytes; the sole intentional mutable state is one atomically replaced HEAD per derived session key plus bounded lock and temporary housekeeping
effects.process: none; no subprocess, shell, executable lookup, signal handler, dynamic import, environment read, clock, randomness API, CLI, MCP, transport, or background worker is used
effects.solver: none; the adapter invokes only the accepted pure problem-session replay boundary and never invokes a producer, solver, planner, checker, proof assistant, capability registry, or retry engine

ensures: persist_problem_session prepares and validates the root, derives the session directory solely from full SHA-256 of the validated session ID, acquires one exclusive per-session lock, reloads the exact committed head if present, and calls transition_problem_session with the complete loaded event and artifact bytes plus the new command before writing state.

A create_session command commits only when no head exists. Every later command must name the exact loaded head; stale expected heads, a busy writer lock, command conflicts, invalid or exhausted core results, and cross-session state return or raise a classified refusal without replacing the prior head.

Every command, event, revision, externally supplied artifact, and immutable store-head manifest is written to fan-out content paths derived only from its full lowercase SHA-256. Existing objects are accepted only when their exact bytes, size, regular-file type, single-link count, owner where enforceable, and read-only mode match.

New immutable objects are written through same-directory temporary regular files, fully flushed and fsynced where supported, installed without overwriting an existing content identity, sealed read-only, and directory-synced before any mutable head change. Hash collisions, link races, size drift, and differing existing bytes fail closed.

The mutable HEAD file contains only one canonical store-head envelope whose self hash, session key, revision, exact core revision identity, complete ordered event inventory, complete sorted artifact inventory, and contract bindings recompute. HEAD replacement uses a same-directory temporary file, flush, fsync, atomic os.replace, and directory fsync while the lock is held.

An interrupted write before HEAD replacement leaves the previous valid head authoritative for storage replay; newly installed but unreferenced immutable objects and temporary files never count as committed history. An interrupted write after atomic replacement yields the complete new head because all referenced immutable objects were durably installed first.

load_problem_session(root: Path, session_id: str) reads one exact HEAD and only its bounded referenced content objects, rejects links, aliases, ownership or mode drift, missing, surplus, writable, corrupted, or noncanonical state, and calls transition_problem_session with command None for fresh complete replay before returning an unchanged result.

recover_problem_session_store(root: Path, session_id: str) never invents or rolls forward a head: under an exclusive recovery lock it removes only bounded adapter-named temporary files and a previously abandoned lock, then returns the freshly replayed last committed head or a classified missing-state refusal. It never deletes immutable content objects or a valid HEAD.

Exact immediate command retry is idempotent: the core returns unchanged and the adapter leaves the same HEAD bytes and identity. A successful new update returns the exact core updated result whose head and revision match the freshly reloaded committed store head.

Filesystem persistence never grants or preserves authority by itself. Loads replay structure but do not rerun attempts, producers, solvers, planners, or proof assistants; mathematical_authority remains false and retained evidence tiers remain subject to their own accepted checker and provenance contracts.
MemoryError, KeyboardInterrupt, and SystemExit propagate after best-effort descriptor and lock cleanup and are never converted into committed success, replay validity, or authority.

epistemics.committed: one structurally replayable non-authoritative core revision is referenced by an atomically installed exact HEAD; this is storage durability, not mathematical truth
epistemics.conflict: the expected head, lock state, command identity, or replayed session differs; the prior head remains the only committed state
epistemics.invalid: path, object, head, history, artifact, or core replay validation failed; no new head or authority is produced
epistemics.missing: no committed replayable head exists for the exact session ID; orphan content is not promoted
epistemics.non_authoritative: filesystem persistence, ownership, immutability, hashing, replay, and recovery never create mathematical authority
epistemics.recovered: bounded uncommitted adapter temporaries or an externally confirmed abandoned lock were removed while the last valid head and immutable objects remained unchanged

invariants: The adapter carries exactly one top-level MH-C-PROBLEM-SESSION-STORE-001 identity and accepted hash, imports the accepted pure core in one direction only, and the pure core never imports this module or any filesystem owner.

The store root is a non-root absolute pathlib.Path with no parent traversal. Every existing path component is inspected without following links and every derived child name is fixed text or lowercase full SHA-256 without separators, dots, aliases, or mixed case.

The directory layout is objects/HH/rest for exact content, sessions/HH/rest/HEAD for the sole mutable pointer, and adapter-prefixed same-directory temporary and lock entries; no user-supplied relative name is joined.

Committed content is a single-link, regular, exact-owner where enforceable, read-only file whose size and full SHA-256 are checked before and after descriptor-based reading. Symlinks, reparse points, hard links, devices, sockets, writable objects, and changed inodes fail closed.

A HEAD is accepted only when its session ID hashes to its directory, its contract bindings and self hash are exact, every listed event and artifact object exists once, no referenced identity is duplicated, and fresh core replay reproduces the same revision and head.

The per-session writer lock is acquired without replacement and released only by its holder during ordinary completion. Busy locks never trigger waiting, stealing, PID lookup, age comparison, or automatic recovery.

No HEAD is created or replaced for core conflict, invalid, or exhausted output, a stale expected head, incomplete object installation, failed fsync before replacement, hash collision, link or ownership drift, or an exception before commit.

Recovery requires explicit caller coordination, removes only exact adapter-prefixed uncommitted files within the selected session directory, never scans outside bounded derived directories, and never removes an immutable object or committed HEAD.

Store load and post-commit verification always invoke pure replay from exact bytes and compare the complete revision. Persisted result bytes, file names, directory order, modes, and caller claims are not replay authority.

Identical updates deduplicate immutable objects and preserve the exact HEAD; divergent same-parent writers yield one commit and one deterministic conflict among cooperating writers without history overwrite or merge.

The adapter provides same-host filesystem atomicity for cooperating writers, not distributed consensus, network replication, encryption, access-control policy, garbage collection, remote synchronization, branch merging, or multi-host locking.
No persistence outcome implies a lemma is true, an obligation is mathematically discharged, evidence is fresh, a context is consistent, or a solver result is trusted.
raises: ProblemSessionStoreError with kind type, path, missing, exists, lock, ownership, mode, link, collision, mutation, partial, head, replay, conflict, budget, or io is raised for ordinary adapter refusals; no such exception implies a new head was committed.

Core conflict, invalid, and exhausted ProblemSessionResult outcomes are returned without persistence; a core updated or unchanged result is never returned until the corresponding current store head has been freshly loaded and replayed.

PermissionError is raised when host permissions deny a required operation and cannot be safely classified before opening; unsupported filesystem durability features may be recorded as best-effort only when atomic replacement and exact content verification still succeed.
MemoryError, KeyboardInterrupt, and SystemExit propagate and never become ordinary persistence outcomes.
requires: The accepted MH-C-WORKFLOW-001=99cfdf17371938af65c4203c02cbaac0bf73470e9fab59f7a6d62360fc0b7cca and MH-C-PROBLEM-SESSION-001=822f72c9f41f583e4e0535e83b9dbb10954202acc820192e52eab48a5c2d9c0a govern this non-authoritative filesystem adapter.

The canonical mutable head envelope is governed by docs/contracts/schemas/problem-session-store-head-v1.schema.json=a5bed15dda9e8c229687f1a89ba1ca9770e17d72314d16b5de63417472f3f683; all persisted events, artifacts, revisions, commands, and result meanings remain governed by the eleven MH-C-PROBLEM-SESSION-001 schema bindings.

root is an exact pathlib.Path naming a non-root absolute path beneath a caller-owned storage location. The explicit root and every existing ancestor or component are real directories rather than symlinks, reparse points, files, or caller-supplied relative traversal.

command is exact built-in bytes for one canonical problem-session command and artifacts is an exact built-in tuple of exact built-in bytes. The command session ID and expected head are the only mutable-head selectors; callers never provide relative object, event, session, lock, temporary, or head paths.

Writers using this adapter cooperate through the same per-session exclusive lock. Recovery of a crashed writer is explicitly requested only after external coordination has established that no writer is live; load remains read-only and ignores uncommitted lock or temporary state.
signature: persist_problem_session(root: Path, command: bytes, artifacts: tuple[bytes, ...]) -> ProblemSessionResult
